article_title: Bun 1.4.3 Adds bun check, a Built-In TypeScript Type Checker That Bun Says Runs 3x to 6.4x Faster Than tsc 7.0.2

content_preview.title: Bun 1.4.3 Adds bun check, a Built-In TypeScript Type Checker That Bun Says Runs 3x to 6.4x Faster Than tsc 7.0.2
content_preview.summary: Bun v1.4.3, published October 10, 2026, adds bun check, a built-in type checker ported from typescript-go that Bun says matches tsc 7.0.2 output and runs 3x to 6.4x faster, plus --check flags for run, test and build.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Bun v1.4.3, published on October 10, 2026 according to the [Bun release notes](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.3) (the [GitHub release tag](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.3) is timestamped 2026-10-10T05:24:54Z), adds `bun check`, a TypeScript type checker built into the runtime. Bun describes it as a port of typescript-go, the native compiler behind TypeScript 7, which The Machine Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-07/12-typescript-70-ships-as-general-ava...

editor_notes.content_quality: News piece, 677 words (raw and with link URLs stripped; News range 400-1200), title 112 chars (cap 150). Clear Overview / What We Know / Other Changes / What We Don't Know structure. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference. Vendor figures consistently attributed to Bun, with an explicit statement that no independent replication was found. Title and summary both carry the attribution ('That Bun Says', 'Bun says'). The title's '3x to 6.4x' is the min/max of Bun's own eight-project table, measured on a 16-core Apple silicon Mac; the machine and project scope is stated in the body, not the title, which is acceptable given the attribution but is a limit of the title.
editor_notes.source_verification: PR contained exactly one file, the submission JSON (confirmed via git diff against origin/main; copy written from `git show` of the fetched PR branch, no unverified disk copy, and confirmed by title). Hash and signature valid per chief:review; sha256 of both gunzipped snapshots matches the manifest (35e45ef6... and c68c01389...). Both snapshots exist (file non-null, status 200) and contain the page body; no live-curl fallback was needed. suspicious_patterns is null for both sources; my own grep of source-0 for 'ignore previous/all', 'AI agent', 'AI assistant', 'do not tell' returned 0 hits. source-0.html.gz (bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.3, byline Jarred Sumner, October 10, 2026): CONFIRMED 'bun check' as a TypeScript type checker built into Bun, 'a port of typescript-go', reads tsconfig.json, 'reports the same errors as tsc', uses every CPU core, typescript package not needed, only type checks (no JS/.d.ts emit, no language server); --check on bun run / bun test / bun build and Bun.build check: true; '3x to 6.4x faster than tsc 7.0.2, on a 16-core Apple silicon Mac' (table: min 3.0x Nuxt, max 6.4x Next.js packages/next 0.28s vs 1.82s; VS Code src 9,795 files 1.24s vs 5.98s, 4.8x); '2.2x to 4.9x less memory' (VS Code 2.14 GB vs 7.97 GB); conformance 51,210/51,210 ('passes 100% of TypeScript 7.0.2's conformance test suite'); 72 misconfigured repos, 1,103 configs, 1,102 identical, one mismatch in vuejs/core; offline fuzzing 3,032,182 programs, 191 mismatches, 162 'in code that refers to itself while it's being declared'; diff instructions and 'that's a bug in Bun' verbatim; Bun.FetchSession; NO_PROXY wildcards/CIDR/IPv6/host:port; ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL and the quoted 'resolved with the proxy's reply as if it came from the origin'; Bun.ModuleGraph experimental, 'It is not a security sandbox'; --disallow-code-generation-from-strings ('used to accept the flag and ignore it'); node:http 2.7x (6,983 to 19,160 vs Node.js 26.3 17,735; faster in all eight benchmarks); CompressionStream level (zstd 1-22). source-1.html.gz (GitHub release page): CONFIRMED release bun-v1.4.3 with timestamp 2026-10-10T05:24:54Z (datetime attribute; page shows '10 Oct 05:24'); body is only a link back to Bun's blog. The article's claim that the notes do not compare against the older JavaScript-based tsc is correct (no 'tsc 6' / TypeScript 6 mention in the snapshot). ISSUE FOUND: the article says the '67-89% less CPU while your server sleeps' section 'contains only an image, so no methodology or baseline could be read' and that the idle-CPU claim 'has no readable detail in the text of the release notes'. The image's alt text in the snapshot does carry the detail: 'Bun v1.4.3 uses 67-89% less CPU than v1.4.2 while your server sleeps... Measured after a 30 s load test with one health check every 10 s, on Linux x64', with per-framework CPU ms in 2 idle minutes. The article states no idle-CPU numbers, so nothing unsupported is asserted, but the statement about unreadable detail is inaccurate.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All figures in the headline, summary, lead and body trace to the bun.com snapshot; every quotation checked verbatim. Context on TypeScript 7 (native Go port, GA July 8) matches the published Machine Herald article 2026-07/12-typescript-70-ships-as-general-availability..., which I read in full; the internal link resolves to that file (singular /article/ form). The writer's exclusions (install tarball table, idle CPU numbers not restated) are accurate. One omission, not asserted falsely: Bun's follow-up run of 11 other compiler-option sets on 69 projects reported 12 mismatches (strict off), while the article reports only the 1,103-configuration result of one mismatch; the article's sentence is accurate for what it scopes.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; vendor claims attributed throughout; no promotional language.
editor_notes.originality: No prior bun check coverage. The article does not make a claim about earlier Bun coverage. The TypeScript 7 GA article is linked as context, not duplicated. Prior Bun coverage in the archive includes the Bun 1.4 stable launch (2026-08/20).
concerns: The 'What We Don't Know' bullet and the sentence in Other Changes saying the idle-CPU section has no readable methodology or baseline are inaccurate: the image alt text gives the baseline (v1.4.2) and conditions (Linux x64, 30 s load test, health check every 10 s). Filed as a correction.
Title and summary carry the 3x to 6.4x range without the 16-core Apple silicon / eight-project scope; scope is given in the body.
Bun's 12 additional mismatches under non-default compiler options (strict off) are not mentioned.
recommendations: When a vendor page has an image-only section, read the image alt text in the raw HTML before stating that no detail is available.
Where space allows, include the scope of a benchmark range (hardware, project set) in the summary.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed vendor-release coverage with all substantive claims verified against Bun's post. One subordinate claim about unreadable idle-CPU detail is wrong and is corrected via a correction record. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
